stories.title: Bitcoin Holds Steady as South Korea's AI Stock Crash Wipes Out $800 Million in Crypto
stories.summary: A crash in South Korea's AI stock market triggered an $800 million wipeout across crypto markets. Bitcoin held its price despite the sell-off. Other crypto assets took a bigger hit than Bitcoin did.
stories.whyItMatters: The gap between Bitcoin and other assets during this sell-off tests whether Bitcoin is decoupling from riskier markets under stress.
whatToWatch: Whether Bitcoin keeps its level if the South Korean sell-off spreads further.
Any follow-on moves in altcoins or leveraged crypto positions.
questions: What exactly caused the $800 million wipeout?
Is this decoupling a lasting pattern or a one-day event?

sources.title: Bitcoin defies $800 million crypto wipeout as South Korea’s AI stock market crashes

stories.title: Quantum-Safe Bitcoin Protection Gets 82% Cheaper as Researchers Race to Secure 6 Million Exposed BTC
stories.summary: Researchers cut the cost of quantum-safe protection for Bitcoin by 82%. The lower cost targets an estimated 6 million BTC seen as exposed to future quantum computing attacks. The report frames the work as a race against the pace of quantum computing progress.
stories.whyItMatters: Quantum computing could eventually break the cryptography that secures Bitcoin wallets, so cheaper protection matters for the network's long-term safety.
whatToWatch: How fast holders and wallets adopt the cheaper quantum-safe methods.
Any new estimates on when quantum computing could threaten Bitcoin.
questions: How was the 6 million BTC exposure figure calculated?
Who is leading or funding this research?

sources.title: Bitcoin’s quantum-safe protection gets 82% cheaper as researchers race to secure 6 million exposed BTC

stories.title: Ethereum Name Service Plans Major .eth Overhaul With One Irreversible Catch
stories.summary: Ethereum Name Service (ENS) plans a major overhaul of its .eth domain system. The plan includes one irreversible change for existing domain holders. Full details on the mechanics are not yet clear.
stories.whyItMatters: ENS domains are widely used for identity and wallet naming on Ethereum, so an irreversible change affects a large base of holders.
whatToWatch: ENS's official rollout timeline for the overhaul.
Guidance for holders on how to handle the irreversible step.
questions: What part of the change is irreversible, and can holders opt out?
Will the overhaul affect domain pricing or renewal terms?

sources.title: Ethereum Name Service plans major .eth overhaul with one irreversible catch for domain holders

stories.title: Ledger Wallet Implant Scare Triggers Trezor Reseller Crackdown
stories.summary: A scare over an alleged implant in Ledger hardware wallets has spread security concerns across the market. Trezor responded with a crackdown on its resellers. The episode points to supply-chain risk as a concern for hardware wallet makers.
stories.whyItMatters: Hardware wallets are a core defense for crypto holders, so supply-chain tampering fears can shake trust across the whole category.
whatToWatch: Official statements from Ledger addressing the implant claims.
Whether other wallet makers tighten reseller vetting too.
questions: Has the implant claim been confirmed, or is it still unverified?
Which resellers does the Trezor crackdown actually affect?

sources.title: Ledger’s crypto wallet implant scare triggers Trezor reseller crackdown as security fears spread

stories.title: Australia Moves to Close Crypto Derivatives Loophole After A$458 Million in Retail Losses
stories.summary: Australian regulators are acting to close a loophole in crypto derivatives rules. The move follows A$458 million in losses by retail traders. The loophole reportedly let some products skip standard investor protections.
stories.whyItMatters: Tighter rules could cut retail losses, but they may also limit access to leveraged crypto products for Australian traders.
whatToWatch: The timeline for Australia's new derivatives rules.
How crypto derivatives providers respond to the change.
questions: What exact loophole allowed these losses?
Will the new rules apply retroactively or only from now on?

sources.title: Australia moves to close crypto derivatives loophole after retail traders lose A$458 million

stories.title: Strategy Spent Nearly 9x More on STRC Buybacks Than on Bitcoin Last Week
stories.summary: Strategy spent close to nine times more cash buying back its STRC shares than buying Bitcoin last week. This marks a notable shift in how the company allocated capital. Strategy remains one of the largest corporate holders of Bitcoin.
stories.whyItMatters: Strategy's buying pattern is widely watched as a signal of institutional Bitcoin demand, so a pullback in BTC purchases stands out.
whatToWatch: Whether this buyback-heavy pattern continues in coming weeks.
Any slowdown in the growth rate of Strategy's total Bitcoin holdings.
questions: Why did Strategy favor STRC buybacks over Bitcoin purchases this week?
Does this mark a change in its long-term Bitcoin accumulation plan?

sources.title: Strategy spent nearly nine times as much on STRC buybacks as Bitcoin last week

stories.title: South Korea Clears the Way for Courts to Seize and Sell Bitcoin for Unpaid Debts
stories.summary: South Korea set new rules, due to start in November, that let courts seize and sell Bitcoin to cover unpaid debts. The rules formally treat Bitcoin as an asset courts can claim in debt enforcement. This follows wider use of crypto as a store of wealth in the country.
stories.whyItMatters: The rules set a precedent for how courts treat crypto in debt collection, which other countries may watch or follow.
whatToWatch: The November start date for the new enforcement rules.
How courts handle valuation and sale of seized Bitcoin.
questions: How will courts value Bitcoin at seizure versus at sale?
Will the rule extend to other crypto assets beyond Bitcoin?

sources.title: South Korea clears way for courts to seize and sell Bitcoin for unpaid debts under new November rules

stories.title: UK Court Rules Being Defrauded Isn't Enough to Claim a Disputed $5 Billion Bitcoin Fortune
stories.summary: A UK court ruled that a fraud claim alone does not entitle a party to a disputed $5 billion Bitcoin fortune. The ruling leaves the question of ownership open. The case shows how hard it is to recover crypto through the courts.
stories.whyItMatters: The ruling sets a legal bar for crypto fraud claims in the UK, shaping how victims can pursue stolen or disputed digital assets.
whatToWatch: Any appeal or further court proceedings in the case.
What evidence standard the court says a claimant must meet.
questions: Who are the parties disputing ownership of the $5 billion?
What proof would satisfy the court beyond a fraud claim?

sources.title: A $5 billion Bitcoin fortune is at stake, but UK court says being defrauded isn’t enough to claim it

stories.title: Sky's $4.4 Billion Liquidity Disclosure Shows Why USDS Cash-Outs Need a Separate Bank Route
stories.summary: Sky, the protocol formerly known as MakerDAO, disclosed $4.4 billion in liquidity. The disclosure shows that cashing out its USDS stablecoin needs a separate banking route outside normal on-chain mechanisms. This points to how much traditional banking still underpins stablecoin redemption.
stories.whyItMatters: Redemption pathways are a key test of stablecoin resilience, especially when holders need to convert large sums to cash.
whatToWatch: Whether Sky adds or changes banking partners for USDS redemption.
Any stress event that tests USDS liquidity at scale.
questions: Which bank or banks handle the separate redemption route?
How does this liquidity compare with USDS's total supply?

sources.title: Sky’s $4.4 billion liquidity disclosure shows why USDS cash-outs need a separate bank route

stories.title: More Than Half of Ethena's USDe Backing Is Allocated to Lending
stories.summary: A new breakdown shows that over half of the assets backing Ethena's USDe stablecoin now sit in lending allocations. This shifts the backing away from the delta-neutral trading strategy USDe was originally built on. The change raises questions about the risk behind the token.
stories.whyItMatters: USDe was pitched on a specific hedging strategy, so a heavy tilt toward lending changes the risk holders are exposed to.
whatToWatch: Any official response from Ethena on the backing mix.
Changes in USDe's yield or peg stability tied to this shift.
questions: Which lending counterparties or platforms hold this allocation?
Does this change Ethena's risk disclosures to users?

sources.title: More than half of Ethena’s USDe backing is allocated to lending
